full_judgment:
55. In spite of the presumption of truth attached to oral evidence under oath if the Court is not satisfied, the evidence in spite of oath is of no avail. 

 63. It is well settled that when it is established that the husband and wife were residing in the same house at the relevant time, the husband is duty bound to explain the circumstances how his wife met her death and in absence of any explanation coming from the husband, irresistible presumption is that it is the husband who is responsible for her death. In this regard reliance can be placed in the case of State Vs. Aynul Huq 9 MLR 393= 9 BLC 529. This view receives support in the case of Gouranga Kumar Saha vs. State 2 BLC (AD) 126. Abdul Mutaleb Howlader vs. State 5 MLR (AD)92= 6 BLC(AD)1, Dipok Kumar Sarkar vs. State reported in 40 DLR(AD) 139 and Sudhir Kumar Das alias Khudi Vs. State 60 DLR- 261.
